steps.scene: Ahead is a rectangular sign — a plain oblong, not a triangle or a circle.

question.prompt: What does the rectangle shape tell you to expect?

options.text: Information or directions
An order you must obey
A hazard warning

question.explanation: Rectangles inform or direct. Triangles warn and circles order — the oblong tells you what's there or where to go.

a.label: Green
a.body: Primary route direction sign — the main roads between towns.

b.label: Brown
b.body: Tourist information — attractions and visitor facilities.

question.prompt: A brown rectangular sign with white symbols shows…

options.text: A hazard at the attraction
Directions to a tourist attraction
An order for tourist coaches only

question.explanation: Brown signs give tourist directions and information. Green is for primary routes; brown never warns of danger.

question.prompt: A blue rectangular sign showing a white letter P means…

options.text: Parking is available here or ahead
No parking — keep moving
Police station ahead

question.explanation: A blue sign with a white P points you to parking. A parking ban is a red-and-blue circular sign, not this.

steps.title: Diversion route
steps.body: A diversion sign marks a temporary route around a road closure ahead. Follow it until the normal road resumes.

question.prompt: A sign marked 'Diversion' with a symbol tells you…

options.text: A permanent new main road opens here
Follow a temporary route around a closure
This route is for lorries only

question.explanation: Diversions are temporary — they route you around roadworks or a closure, then hand you back to the normal road.

steps.title: Centre lines
steps.body: A broken white line down the middle of the road separates traffic flowing in opposite directions. Longer marks mean a greater hazard.

question.prompt: A broken white line down the middle of the road…

options.text: Separates lanes travelling the same way
Separates traffic going in opposite directions
Means no stopping at any time

question.explanation: The centre line divides opposing flows. Lanes going the same way are divided by lane lines, not the centre line.

steps.title: Double white lines
steps.body: Where the white line nearest you is solid, you must not cross or straddle it to overtake. Wait until it becomes broken and it's safe.

question.prompt: The white line nearest you is solid (double white lines). You…

options.text: May cross it whenever the road ahead looks clear
Must not cross or straddle it to overtake
May cross it only after dark

question.explanation: A solid line nearest you means no crossing to overtake — wait until it becomes broken and the way is clear.

steps.wrongBelief: Road markings are only guidance, not rules you can be penalised for.

options.text: It's right — only signs are enforceable
Many markings are legal orders — stop lines, box junctions, solid whites
Markings only matter inside towns

question.explanation: Plenty of markings carry the force of law: stop lines, box junctions and solid white lines can all bring a penalty.

steps.repairNote: Road markings can be as binding as signs — a stop line, box junction or solid white line is a legal order, not advice.
